class_id: one Redis instance shared by prod and staging with unprefixed keys
feature: the Redis cache/lock layer every slot connects to (web/lib/cache/redis-client.ts, scraper's cycle lock, packages/shared cache keys)
symptom: prod and staging point at the same Redis host, port and logical DB (127.0.0.1:6379, db 0, no per-slot index) with unprefixed keys, including the scraper's own cycle lock (`lock:resource:scraper:cycle`). Any staging write, cache warm, or lock acquire/release can silently read, overwrite or unlock a prod key and vice versa: a staging cycle can block a prod wake by holding prod's lock name, a staging deploy's lock release can delete prod's in-flight lock, and staging-derived cache values have been served to prod readers. Universal shape: two environments sharing one keyspace with no prefix or index separation turn every cache/lock name into a cross-environment collision, not a config nicety.
first_seen: #151 (2026-08-22, T-263 deploy verification): a staging listing-performance write was immediately served back on prod's public API with the staging write's exact timestamp, while prod's own Postgres row was still stale. 2026-09-26 read confirms every slot's REDIS_URL is still 127.0.0.1:6379 with no db index, including the shared scraper cycle lock key `lock:resource:scraper:cycle`.
fix_prs: #1155 (parked, run-discipline A1 after two Tier A rounds): every Redis key prefixed prod:/staging:/db-<name>: derived from the connected database, all four client factories updated (incl. KEYS/SCAN), per-slot cycle locks plus one deliberate shared box:lock:resource:extractor (keeps the W-178 guard the old shared lock gave by accident), build-time reject-all stub, rollback script for unprefixed keys, CI grep blocking a Redis client created outside the factories. See #151 comments for full state.
detection_check: none yet -- no nightly check currently asserts Redis key/slot separation; extending shared/bin/assert-slot-dsn.sh (which already asserts Postgres DSN separation between slots) to also assert Redis DB-index or prefix separation is the suggested detection upgrade, not yet built
